title: 7 Ways to WOW your Client: An Experienced PM's Guide
author: The Effective Project Manager
summary: This practitioner guide argues that successful delivery does not guarantee a delighted client, and that clients who are merely neutral are less likely to rehire you and may speak badly of you. The author frames client satisfaction as deliberate practice rather than mystique and offers seven strategies: build trust through relationships, exceed expectations, deliver quality, meet deadlines and budgets, be transparent, work flexibly in an agile way, and manage risk proactively. Recurring themes are communicating problems before they surprise the client, soliciting feedback early, involving the client in decisions so they own the outcome, and giving them a senior contact. The advice is general rather than novel, but it is coherent client and stakeholder leadership practice.
points: Delivering a successful project is not enough, because clients remember struggles and neutral clients rarely rehire or recommend.
Trust comes from setting clear expectations early and soliciting feedback proactively so criticism reaches you directly rather than behind your back.
Involving clients in decisions builds ownership and reduces objection to ideas they helped create.
Early, honest communication about risks, delays and budget issues is less damaging than surprises.
Visible senior attention and celebrating team successes reassure clients and sustain team morale.
quotes: The project manager is faced with a problem. Project success does not always result in exuberance from the client. At best they are satisfied.
When the client is not impressed, they are much less likely to hire you for more work. They may even speak negatively of you and your team to their associates or your seniors at your organisation.

The cornerstone of any successful client relationship is trust. This trust is built through open and honest communication, frequent interaction, and a genuine commitment to understanding and addressing client needs.

Regularly solicit client feedback through surveys, interviews, and informal conversations. This allows you to address concerns proactively and make adjustments as needed. It also shows that you are open to constructive criticism.
Nothing erodes client trust faster than missed deadlines and budget overruns. Develop a realistic project plan and stick to it.

Be open and honest about project challenges and opportunities. Address concerns promptly and proactively to minimize uncertainty and anxiety. A problem clearly communicated is less stressful than a problem which surprises the client.

Also let the client know that a more senior member of your company is also available to assist them. The client will be reassured, and impressed, that their status is important enough to warrant attention from senior management.
